scope: Paper 4 Stage 0-9 academic/content completeness after the Stage 9 Python/theory post-release audit
release_boundary: This review does not modify the app, Stage 9 status, or any historical release artifact.

stage_assessment.finding: The contract correctly requires theory, source locators, Python, trace, output/test, evidence, marking integrity, and full VI/EN parity.
The 2021-2025 corpus is a usable verified baseline: 29 QP/MS pairs, 87 questions, and 672 scored parts.
The 58-pattern taxonomy covers all 672 scored parts; 20 limited-evidence patterns remain explicitly identified.
The source model is strong but explicitly marked PLANNED_NOT_AUTHORED. Its 108 knowledge blocks and direct book/objective joins were not carried into the published registry.
All 58 patterns have method and marking design, but the app exposes direct QP/MS marking references in only 12 of 26 marking blocks, covering 32 of 58 lesson pattern IDs.
Execution evidence exists for 4,881 obligations, but no published lesson example points to a Stage 5 author run or independent rerun.
Coverage accounting passed, while knowledge was flattened to one short summary per lesson and assessment requirement IDs were not preserved in the final learning objects.
The event model is suitable for state changes but must resolve code-line references to the actual published Python example.
The runtime covers 58 patterns, 174 scenarios, and 331 events. It does not prove theory depth or Python execution provenance.
Semantic Python rendering is now present for 26 of 26 lessons, but source, theory, execution, assessment, marking, and full bilingual acceptance remain open.

risks.risk: Flattening or regenerating the registry can again discard stable source IDs and structured knowledge.
risks.control: Make source joins typed and validator-enforced before authoring starts.

risks.risk: Displayed snippets can diverge from Stage 5 programs while retaining a generic runnable claim.
risks.control: Hash the exact displayed source and bind that hash to an independent run record.

risks.risk: Editorial advice can be presented as an official Cambridge marking point.
risks.control: Require authority class and exact atom locator on every marking chain.

risks.risk: VI/EN can have matching top-level keys while examples, table rows, or event state differ semantically.
risks.control: Use one locale-neutral data object plus localized prose and run structural and human semantic parity checks.

risks.risk: Expanding to 108 blocks can make pages unusably long and hide code again.
risks.control: Use indexed sub-sections, progressive disclosure, and direct anchors while preserving all knowledge IDs.

risks.risk: Historical RELEASE_LOCKED artifacts may be mistaken for the current decision.
risks.control: Keep Stage 9 REWORK_REQUIRED authoritative and issue a new release ID only after W7.

lead_decision_rules: Do not restart or rewrite Stages 0-5 wholesale; consume their verified artifacts through explicit joins.
Do not advance a batch when a denominator is reduced, an authority is ambiguous, or independent evidence is missing.
Treat a passing build as necessary but insufficient for academic acceptance.
Require independent QA by an agent that did not author the inspected batch.
Keep Stage 9 in REWORK_REQUIRED until W7 produces a replacement manifest.
